title.narrative: Civil Rights Defenders Ethiopia, Phase II 2023-2025
Civil Rights Defenders Etiopien, Fas II 2023-2025

description.narrative: Insatsens övergripande mål är att skapa förutsättningar för människorättsarbete genom att öka säkerheten och den organisatoriska kapaciteten hos människorättsförsvarare, intensifiera arbetet för unga och kvinnliga människorättsförsvarare, rehabilitering av civilsamhället i konfliktdrabbade områden, och stärkt kapacitet att övervaka kränkningar av mänskliga rättigheter.

The overall objective (s) of the contribution is creating enabling environment for human rights work through increasing safety and organisational capacity of human rights defenders (HRDs), intensifying the work of young and women human rights defenders, rehabilitation of civil society in conflict-affected areas, and strengthened capacity to monitor violations of human rights.

Outcome 1: A vibrant civic space with resilient, capable, and impactful human rights organizations and human rights defenders Outcome 2: Human rights organizations engage in efforts to bring accountability for human rights violations. Outcome 3: HRDs have safety and security to conduct impactful human rights work. Outcome 4: Human rights organizations and HRDs will be able to influence core agenda of the national dialogue process.

The program reports the following major results in the narrative report for the period 1 June-31 Dec 2022: (UM2023/05992/ADDI-30):
1. Human rights organizations are receiving necessary support to enhance their resilience of the civic space by strengthening their organizational capacity. 2. Human rights organizations are engaging in activities and efforts to bring accountability for human rights violations. 3. HRDs are increasing their safety and security through in-depth digital security trainings.
It´s noted that as this program phase is in its initial stages, the report only provides for short term outputs/results and focuses more on the status of each planned activity. Some of these examples are:
-CRD has conducted a comprehensive assessment of its partners latest status and priorities to identify the best possible area and modality of partnership within the scope of the new programme phase.
- The selection on which organizations which will acquire interns was assessed and decided. To the selected six partners, CRD awarded grants to recruit 10 young women interns within their organization. The young women interns are all fresh graduates with zero to some work experience that have shown interest and commitment towards human rights. The interns have different educational background which will be beneficial to the organizations that hired them as well as the sector.
-CRD has provided grants to three partner organizations to conduct systematic collection and documentation of human rights situations on various areas of focus. A grant for a fourth one is being processed and will be finalized in the next reporting period.
-CRD has provided a legal action grant to Defend the Environment to pursue two strategic litigations for the protection of environmental rights. The partner will litigate cases in Oromia and Southwest Region.
-Civil Rights Defenders has started conducting a Training of Trainers (ToT) on digital security
-CRD and its partners have continued the work from phase I to advocate for a human rights agenda setting in the national dialogue process. This activity built up on the results achieved during that period, which was the production of an engagement guideline. However, by the time the project came into effect, the commission had completed agenda collection. Going forward, CRD will provide grants for human rights organizations to work to ensure human rights are centred into all agendas selected.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
